 Order

This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 07/05/2019 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Shivpuri (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.132/2018, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Shivpuri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The date of accident, issue of negligence and the liability of the respondents are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, due to death of Krishna in the motor accident, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.3,35,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10878 2 MA-4287-2019 4.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellants/claimants have preferred this appeal on the ground that the learned Claims Tribunal passed the impugned award without proper appreciation of law.
It is contended that the compensation awarded is on the lower side.

the deceased- Krishna was aged 7 years healthy student. However, the learned Claims Tribunal failed to consider these aspects and assessed the income of the deceased only to the tune of Rs.
30,000/- per annum, which is extremely low.

sentences.text: Despite this, the Claims Tribunal awarded a total compensation of only Rs.3,35,000/- under all heads, which is grossly inadequate.
Placing reliance on judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Karuna Parmar Vs Prakash Sinha and Ors, 2025 ACJ 1624 and Aarti and Ors.

entities.text: Karuna Parmar Vs Prakash Sinha and Ors, 2025 ACJ 1624
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Vs Udayveer Singh and Ors., 2025 ACJ 2835, income of the deceased must be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act of an unskilled person.
It is further contended that Claims Tribunal has committed error in not awarding reasonable amount of compensation in other conventional heads.
Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded to the claimants.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No. 3/Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
It is an admitted position that the deceased was a minor aged about 7 years and a student, and no direct evidence regarding income has been adduced.
In such circumstances, the notional income is required to be assessed on a reasonable basis.

8. In light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10878 3 MA-4287-2019 o f Aarti & Others (supra) and Karuna Parmar (supra), wherein the income of a minor has been assessed on the basis of minimum wages applicable to an unskilled worker, this Court deems it appropriate to assess the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.7,125/-.

9. As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment o f National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra), future prospects @ 40% be assessed.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 18 be applied.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was a bachelor, deduction of 1/2 towards personal expenses is required.

Further, the parents of the deceased are also entitled to compensation under the head of consortium in view of the law laid down in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Satinder Kaur & Ors. (2020 ACJ 2131).

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Satinder Kaur & Ors. (2020 ACJ 2131)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
10. Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD   Income Rs.7,125  Future Prospects@ 40% Rs.1,19,
 Dependency 1/2 Rs.59,85  Multiplier 18 Rs.10,77 Dheeraj Chourasiya vs Vijay Singh Mahor on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196579176/
2  Other Heads:-
Loss of Consortium (mother and father) Rs.40,000 X 2= 80,000/-
Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
Total Compensation = Rs.11,87,300/-
11.

entities.text: Dheeraj Chourasiya vs Vijay Singh Mahor
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case comes to Rs.11,87,300/- as against the sum of Rs.3,35,000/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are held entitled to an NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:10878 4 MA-4287-2019 additional compensation of Rs.8,52,300/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
12.
In the result, miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned award i s modified, and the compensation is enhanced by a sum of Rs. 8,52,300/-.
The aforesaid enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by Claims Tribunal from the date of deposit of Court fees by the appellants in the present appeal.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

13. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
14. In view of the foregoing, the miscellaneous appeal stands is partly allowed and stands disposed of accordingly.
